packageRules.description: controller-runtime, k8s.io/* and controller-tools must always move as one unit: a mismatch between the client libraries and the API server version breaks envtest and the generated CRDs.

kustomize is held at v5.8.2, and moving it is not a Renovate bump: v5.8.3 (kyaml v0.21.3) requires a newer kube-openapi whose schema conversion moved to structured-merge-diff/v7, which does not type-check against k8s.io/apimachinery (still v6), so `make lint` fails and the image build with it. The Makefile's KUSTOMIZE_VERSION pins the same version and no manager reads the Makefile, so a bot bump would move one copy of the pin and not the other. Moving past v5.8.2 means moving the whole k8s.io/* set, which is a deliberate change (docs/versions.md); re-enable this rule when that happens.
Lint toolchain lives in tools/go.mod as a `tool` directive.
Tool directives in the root module: bump them together with the copies in the Makefile and the Dockerfiles, which the pull request template enforces.
The kind node image must stay on the same Kubernetes minor version as the envtest binaries; a major/minor bump is a deliberate change.

The Go toolchain is one version written in five places: the `go` directive in go.mod and tools/go.mod, the GO_VERSION env in the workflows, the devcontainer image and the build image the Dockerfiles take as GO_IMAGE. One pull request has to move them together, which is what docs/versions.md means by GO_VERSION tracking the `go` directive.

coturn is the relay data plane. The pins Renovate moves are the Makefile pair (`COTURN_IMAGE` with `COTURN_IMAGE_DIGEST`, which `make load-coturn` requires to agree) and the example pool; grouping them means one pull request moves both, tag and digest together. The copies under test/ move by hand with the pin: Renovate's default ignorePaths skips `test/**`, and the e2e default is only a fallback for `make test-e2e`, which passes the Makefile value explicitly (docs/versions.md).

The kubernetes manager also reads apiVersion fields, and the HPA example's `autoscaling/v2` is the manifest API the cluster serves, not a version to track: a newer API only matters when the CRD moves to it on purpose.
ginkgo and gomega move together on a major bump.

The chart's default image tag is its appVersion, the release version (ADR 17), so this file is not a pin any bot should move. `docker:pinDigests` reads `image.repository` plus the empty `tag:` as a docker dependency and writes the digest into the tag — `tag: "@sha256:…"` — which renders `ghcr.io/hazmi35/turnfleet-controller:@sha256:…`, an invalid reference that stops the chart installing. That is what pull request #50 did; the chart follows the release, and the release is the maintainer's act.

kubernetes.description: Scoped to the examples: the kubernetes manager matches no file by default, and the rest of config/ carries only this project's own placeholder image (`controller:latest`), which is not a dependency to track.

customManagers.description: Pin the Go toolchain used by CI: GO_VERSION in .github/workflows. The match includes the `GO_VERSION: "` around the value, so the replacement writes that syntax back instead of a bare version.

The coturn data plane, as the Makefile pins it: the tag and the digest are one dependency, because `make load-coturn` refuses a tag that does not resolve to COTURN_IMAGE_DIGEST, so they can never be bumped apart. The match spans both lines, so the replacement writes both back, variable name and all.

The kind node image, as the Makefile pins it: the only place it is written, so the `kind node image` rule above had nothing to group until now. It has to stay on the Kubernetes minor the envtest binaries use.
The build image, as the Makefile pins it. It carries the Go toolchain (`golang:1.27.2-bookworm`) and the Dockerfiles only say `FROM ${GO_IMAGE}`, so the Makefile is the only place the pin exists.
The runtime base image, as the Makefile pins it: distroless `nonroot` is a tag rather than a version, so this dependency is digest upkeep for a re-pushed tag.

Helm, the chart's renderer and linter, as the Makefile pins it. Helm is not a Go tool, so the version is a Makefile line and the release is downloaded from get.helm.sh by the `helm` target; the `v?` in the match leaves the tag prefix in place when the value is replaced.
